issues.issue: Stray header line 'ALTON original passage' appears before the title and should be removed from the student-facing text.
The vote is the stated exigence but is only lightly gestured at ('whichever way the vote goes'); a clearer mention of the upcoming board vote would sharpen the rhetorical situation.
'Trimmed' understates a cut of roughly 88%; plausibly intentional understatement, but could read as slightly inconsistent with the stakes.
'And yet.' as a standalone pivot and 'The answer is in the handling' are mildly formulaic moves, though they fit the speaker.

In ¶6 'on nine days' notice' misuses the earlier detail: nine days was how long the page took to pass its first goal, not the notice donors were given. The phrase is loose and could confuse a careful reader.
In ¶3 the phrase 'unless we have quietly decided that deserving means...' is slightly muddled in logic, though the parallel gerunds still land.
The planned flaw (Lenore would have disliked this column) appears in ¶6 and is repaired by the next sentence as intended; it only mildly risks the writer's authority and is tolerable.
Stray header label 'ALTON original passage' appears above the letter title and should be removed before the passage ships.

The claim that systems thinking is 'the one habit of mind the rest of the curriculum struggles hardest to deliver' is asserted without support; acceptable for an advocacy letter but slightly sweeping.
Dario's anecdote runs fairly tidy (furious, puzzled, quiet; tax, limit, recovery rule), which is a little neat, though it serves the planned parallelism.
Stray header text 'ALTON original passage' precedes the title and looks like a production artifact; remove before shipping.

Planned flaws are all present and match the blueprint (s3 vague thesis, s5 no acknowledgment of older members, s7 insulting tone, s9 cost without budget framing, s10 missing additive transition, s13 missing concession-response transition). The flaws are noticeable but not so heavy-handed that the draft stops reading as a plausible student/community essay.
The 140-dollar figure is attributed to 'the hardware co-op in Pell,' a fictional local entity. It is plausibly fictional and not presented as a real organization, so this is acceptable.
Stray header text 'ALTON original passage' precedes the title; likely metadata and should be removed before display.
Sentence 10 carries two planned flaws (wordy/casual definition and missing analogy); acceptable but the sentence is very weak, so students must handle both repairs in one place.
Sentence 11 uses 'he or she,' slightly dated phrasing, though harmless for a draft.
Stray header text 'ALTON original passage' appears before the title and should be removed before shipping.
Sentence 3 ('the only person on the stage who makes no sound at all') is a mild overstatement, but it works as a rhetorical hook and is acceptable in a student draft.

Planned flaws (sentences 1, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11) are present and match the blueprint. Sentence 8 and the setup sentences are competent, so the flaws are clearly identifiable and repairable. The claim about breath and gesture is only thinly supported by two anecdotes, which fits the draft-level weakness.
Sentence 5 says 'all forty players' while the orchestra is described as a youth orchestra. This is internally consistent and plausible, so no fix is needed.

Sentence 2 ('Pools are important to communities in many ways') is a generic, stock-sounding filler line that is not in the blueprint's planned flaws. It is tolerable in a draft but slightly weakens the opening.
Sentence 12 contains the duplicated phrase 'the thing I learned is that', which is intended as the planned concision flaw. The repetition is somewhat mechanical but matches the blueprint.
The title and the 'ALTON original passage' header line are metadata-like artifacts and should not appear in the student-facing text.
Stray header text 'ALTON original passage' appears before the title and should be removed from the student-facing passage.
Sentence 12 is deliberately insulting toward readers (planned tone flaw). It is acceptable as a revision target, but it is close to the edge for a school-paper piece addressed to peers.

The opening and some phrasing ('Most people never think about...', 'built by volunteers with shovels') lean slightly toward familiar editorial formula, though overall voice is acceptable for a student draft.
